title: No images at all, text only. Can it still make the same dance? Yes, and with more visual detail
summary: Not a single image uploaded. One block of text is all it takes, and the model regenerates the same dance video with more visual detail than the version that got a first-frame image (7.1 MB vs 3.4 MB). The trade-off: the character's face is no longer pinned frame by frame by that image
tags: Vs the image-first version: 7.1 MB vs 3.4 MB
stats: Uploaded no images at all. Just wrote one text prompt and had the model regenerate a dance video on the same theme, then compared it side by side with the earlier version that was given a first-frame image. Final video: 15.08s · 704×960 (portrait: 704 wide, 960 tall) · 24fps (24 frames per second) · H.264 video + AAC audio

The last version had a first-frame image that nailed the look down. This version has no image to go on, so twin tails, green hair, skirt and the rest of the design have to be spelled out fully and clearly in the prompt (the text you write for the model), all in one go

The audio ships with the video and is generated natively by H3 — picture and sound come out of the same single computation, not music added afterward. The prompt calls out a J-pop dance track + female vocals + audience ambience

Both videos run the exact same node chain (every connection from model loading to final output in the workflow). The only difference is that the MiniMaxH3ImageToVideo node gets no first_frame (first-frame image input): only 'whether it gets a first image' changes, everything else stays as is. This version also has more visual detail: 7.1 MB ▮▮▮▮▮▮, vs 3.4 MB ▮▮▮ for the image-first version
Final video + workflow JSON are archived in experiments/miku-h3-t2v/. One curl command reproduces it, and no file uploads are needed anywhere along the way
findings: More visual detail than the version that got a first-frame image: 7.1 MB vs 3.4 MB. The two versions differ in one thing only — whether they get a first image — so the bigger file means more detail left in the frames. The price: the character's face is no longer pinned frame by frame by the source image and has to hold together through text alone
Very low bar to reproduce: the workflow is archived, one curl command replays it, and no file uploads are needed
That makes 3 generation routes now for this same dance: hand rendering in Blender, H3 with one image first, and H3 with text only (this one)
